To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a generalized autoregreesive pretraining method is better than denoising autoencoder based pretraining for language understanding and (2) Transformer based pretraining outperforms RNN based pretraining.

(1) XLNet, a novel pretraining model, outperforms the state-of-the-art BERT on 19 out of 20 tasks and (2) the pretraining method of XLNet, which maximizes the expected likelihood over a sequence of factorizations, is a promising alternative to the denoising auto-encoding approach of BERT.

1) we introduce a novel pretraining method for NLP that enables learning bidirectional context by maximizing the expected loglikelihood of a sequence over all permutations of factorization order, 2) we demonstrate the superiority of our model over BERT on 11 GLUE tasks and 3) we show that our model outperforms BART on SQuAD v1.1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
two questions.
the question of how to better leverage the power of autoregressive language model for general language understanding and XLNet provides an effective answer.
the following questions. How to learn bidirectional contexts by leveraging the power of autoregressive models?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
XLNet outperformed all the other pre-training approaches on all the tasks.
XLNet outperformed BERT on 12 of the 15 tasks.
XLNet is a generalized autoregreesive pretraining model that outperforms BERN and achieves state-of-the-art results on 20 tasks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a new model for pretraining language representations, XLNet, and we empirically show its effectiveness on a variety of natural language processing tasks.
we present an autoregressive language model that is able to learn bidirectional contextual representation.
XLNet is an improved pretraining method that achieves better performance than BERT.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pretraining objective can be generalized to autoregressive language model, which is a more general class of models that includes both autoencoding and autoregressive language models.
the pretraining-finetuning discrepancy in BERT is not inherent in pretraining methods but rather a result of the unidirectional modeling.
, with an appropriate formulation of autoregressive language model, we can better utilize the power of pretraining for language understanding.
